quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A motorcycle rider without a helmet is ________ more likely to suffer a serious head injury in a crash.
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, a rider is five times more likely to suffer a serious head injury in a crash.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Is not safe for motorcyclists at any time.
Is usually safe for motorcyclists unless it is raining.
Should always be avoided since other parts of the lane do not have oil.
Improves traction for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcyclists unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip in the center of the traffic lane. When the road is dry, this area usually has enough traction for motorcyclists. The strip is often no more than two feet wide, so you can ride to one side and still be in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Guarantees that they will yield to you.
Does not mean that they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean that they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to guarantee that a driver will yield to you. A driver can look directly at a motorcyclist and still fail to notice them.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy for safe riding. What does SEE stand for?
questions.explanation: Experienced riders use the SEE strategy to make safe decisions while riding. SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: How do you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Swerve the bike toward the fewest hazards.
Try to accelerate while the brake is engaged.

questions.explanation: To regain control of a locked rear wheel, you must release the brake. However, if you lock the rear brake on a surface with good grip, you can keep it locked until the motorcycle stops.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, it is usually safest to:
questions.explanation: It is safest to go straight within your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Turning to approach tracks at a right angle is dangerous because it may push you into another lane.

questions.question: To carry a passenger, you may need to adjust:
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight, so you may need to adjust the motorcycle's shocks. You should also adjust the headlight and mirrors because the motorcycle will sit at a different angle with the extra weight.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, you should not:

options.text: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, use both brakes when slowing or stopping. Also reduce your speed and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oily areas, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges, as these are more slippery than others.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light when:

options.text: There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing if someone is following you too closely. The driver may be focused on you and not see the upcoming hazard. Also flash your brake light if you are about to slow down somewhere the driver might not expect it.

questions.question: A motorcycle passenger should:

options.text: Get on before the engine starts.
Get on after the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on after the engine starts.
questions.explanation: Passengers should get on only after the engine has started and the transmission is in neutral. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking the rider's control and should hold onto the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: How much stopping distance do motorcycles need in traffic?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the same stopping distance as cars in traffic.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: A left arm bent at the elbow with the hand pointing up means a right turn. You can use hand signals instead of or along with your turn signals.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly?

options.text: Use the rear brake hard while slowly increasing front brake pressure

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Do you need hearing protection?

options.text: No, not if you wear a helmet
No, not if you are carrying a passenger

questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing even with a helmet. Hearing protection helps while still letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Which is NOT a way to stop a friend from driving while drunk?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them
Keep them busy with activities while they sober up
Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving
Get other friends to help stop them from driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving
questions.explanation: Waiting 15 minutes does not prevent drunk driving. Instead, arrange another way home, keep them busy with other activities, and ask friends for help.

questions.question: When do you NOT need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When there is a lot of traffic
When you can see through the vehicle in front of you

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when the road is slippery, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy. You do not need extra distance when you can see through the vehicle in front.

questions.question: What kind of footwear is proper for riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on rough surfaces. Tuck in laces so they don't get caught.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit
Keep your hand over the clutch and brakes
Shift to neutral when slowing down

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hand over the clutch and brakes
questions.explanation: In dangerous areas like intersections, keep your hand ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should you ride in when preparing to pass on the left?
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of the lane when passing. This gives you a better view ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see the road through vehicles ahead of you.
When the weather is clear and pleasant.

questions.explanation: You should increase your following distance when it takes longer to stop. This includes heavy traffic, bad weather, night driving, or when you cannot see past the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders when looking through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes when looking through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes when looking through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Move only your head and eyes, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Is it a good idea to ride on the far side of a lane behind another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, because drivers will see you easily.
No, because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
Yes, because passengers can tell the driver you are there.
No, because it is illegal to ride anywhere but the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane where the driver is most likely to see you in the rearview mirror.

questions.question: How should you cross railroad tracks that run parallel to the road?
questions.explanation: Cross railroad tracks, trolley tracks, or road seams at least at a 45-degree angle. Make a quick, sharp turn. Crossing at a shallow angle can catch your tires and make you lose control.

questions.question: At what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is a person considered legally intoxicated?
questions.explanation: For adults age 21 and older, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Driving while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.
